# Shop balance and payout history reads

> Shop balances are served from a Redis projection of ledger journals; payout history is queried from the database.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

When money moves through the ledger (see [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md)), a [`JournalPosted`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) event is emitted. The [`BalanceProjector`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/balance.projector.ts#L26) catches these events and applies them to account balances stored in Redis. This denormalized view is fast—a balance read is a single Redis HGET, not a million-row sum—and stays consistent: a Lua script ensures each journal is applied at most once, even if the event is redelivered. When a shop hits `GET /shops/:shopId/balance`, the API reads from the Redis cache; if the projection hasn't caught up yet, it falls back to the authoritative ledger query. The same endpoint also serves payout history: `GET /shops/:shopId/payouts` returns the 52 most recent weekly payouts (created by [Weekly seller payouts](weekly-seller-payouts.md)), ordered by period start date.

**Look at:** [`BalanceProjector` in balance.projector.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/balance.projector.ts#L26) · [`FinanceController` in finance.controller.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/api/finance.controller.ts#L13) · [finance.module.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/finance.module.ts)

## Pieces

- [Redis balance projection from ledger events](balance-projection.md): [`BalanceProjector`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/balance.projector.ts#L26) listens to [`JournalPosted`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) events and applies each journal's lines to a Redis hash of account balances using an atomic Lua script.
- Balance API endpoint: GET /shops/:`shopId`/balance returns the shop's balance from the Redis projection, or queries the ledger if the projection has not yet caught up.
- Payout history API endpoint: GET /shops/:`shopId`/payouts returns the 52 most recent payouts for the shop, ordered by period start date.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | `Redis hash `ledger:balances`` | Account ID → current balance. Updated atomically when [`JournalPosted`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) events are applied; read by the balance endpoint. |
| cache | `Redis keys `ledger:applied:{`journalId`}`` | Idempotency markers that expire after 14 days. Set when a journal is applied; checked by the Lua script to prevent duplicate applications. |
| database | ``Payout` table` | Payout records created by the weekly payout job. Queried and returned by the payouts endpoint; returns the 52 most recent records per shop. |
| event | `Kafka topic ``ledger.journal_posted``` | Consumed by [`BalanceProjector`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/balance.projector.ts#L26) whenever a journal posts. Each event contains the journal ID, lines (account and amount pairs), and metadata. |

## Watch out

- The Redis projection can lag behind the ledger if event processing backlog grows, which is why the balance endpoint has a fallback to the authoritative ledger query.
- The Lua script's SET NX idempotency marker is critical—without it, concurrent redeliveries could double-count the same journal. The marker expires after 14 days (1,209,600 seconds), so it is cheap to store but not forever.
- The balance endpoint returns `source: 'projection' | 'ledger'`, so you can detect when the fast path missed and the slow fallback was used—useful for debugging event processing latency.
- The hot-account problem (everyone writes to the platform fee account) is solved: Redis HINCRBY is atomic, so no row lock contention like a synchronous Postgres balance table would have.
